nodes.summary: Read the CSV file with encoding/csv and trim the header and every value.
nodes.instructions:
Read RFC 4180 CSV with encoding/csv. The first record is the header. Trim leading and trailing
spaces from every header name and every value. Do not reject invalid UTF-8. Blank lines are
skipped by encoding/csv. Keep record line numbers available for diagnostics.
nodes.name: Read the CSV file with encoding/csv and trim the header and every value.

nodes.summary: Report an unopenable or unreadable file, including a directory, with exit 1.
nodes.instructions:
A path that cannot be opened or read, including a missing file and a directory, exits 1 with
nothing on standard output and one diagnostic line on standard error. It must not panic.
nodes.name: Report an unopenable or unreadable file, including a directory, with exit 1.

nodes.summary: Classify empty, NA, N/A, and NULL values as null after trimming.
nodes.instructions:
A trimmed value is null when it is empty or equals NA, N/A, or NULL ignoring case. Every other
value is non-null. Expose the predicate for typing, counts, statistics, and frequencies.
nodes.name: Classify empty, NA, N/A, and NULL values as null after trimming.

nodes.summary: Infer the integer and number column types.
nodes.instructions:
A column is integer when every non-null value matches -?[0-9]+ and number when every non-null
value matches -?[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?. Typing considers only non-null values and picks the first
type in order integer, number, date, boolean, text that all of them satisfy.
nodes.name: Infer the integer and number column types.

nodes.summary: Infer the date column type with real calendar validation.
nodes.instructions:
A column is date when every non-null value matches YYYY-MM-DD and is a real calendar date, so
2025-02-30 is not a date. Use time.Parse with the 2006-01-02 layout plus a strict shape check.
nodes.name: Infer the date column type with real calendar validation.

nodes.summary: Compute the exact median for numeric columns.
nodes.instructions:
Sort the non-null numeric values exactly. The median is the middle value, or the mean of the
two middle values when the count is even, written with two decimals rounded half away from
zero. Other types are blank.
nodes.name: Compute the exact median for numeric columns.

nodes.summary: Count rows, nulls, and distinct non-null values for each column.
nodes.instructions:
rows counts data records, nulls counts null values, and distinct counts different non-null
values compared as exact trimmed strings.
nodes.name: Count rows, nulls, and distinct non-null values for each column.

nodes.summary: Infer the boolean, text, and empty column types.
nodes.instructions:
A column is boolean when every non-null value is true or false ignoring case, text otherwise,
and empty when it has no non-null value.
nodes.name: Infer the boolean, text, and empty column types.

nodes.summary: Compute exact sum and mean for numeric columns, rounded once half away from zero.
nodes.instructions:
Use math/big (big.Rat) for exact arithmetic. integer sum is a plain integer. number sum and
mean are written with two decimals, rounded once half away from zero from the exact value,
with a leading - when negative and no thousands separator. mean is the total divided by the
non-null count; integer mean is also two decimals. Other types are blank.
nodes.name: Compute exact sum and mean for numeric columns, rounded once half away from zero.

nodes.summary: Report min and max for every column type.
nodes.instructions:
integer and number compare numerically using exact math/big values and are written as plain
integers or two-decimal numbers. date gives earliest and latest. boolean gives false if any
value is false else true for min, and true if any value is true else false for max. text
compares by byte value. empty is blank.
nodes.name: Report min and max for every column type.

nodes.summary: Reject empty, malformed, or ragged files with exit 3 and a diagnostic on standard error.
nodes.instructions:
Reject an empty file, an empty or repeated header name, and any record whose field count differs
from the header. Exit 3, write nothing to standard output, and write one standard error line
naming the file and, for a record, its line number. A csv.ParseError is also a rejection.
nodes.name: Reject empty, malformed, or ragged files with exit 3 and a diagnostic on standard error.

nodes.summary: Parse arguments and reject malformed usage with exit 2 and a usage line.
nodes.instructions:
Use a local flag.FlagSet with flag.ContinueOnError and discarded flag output. Options precede
the file. Exit 2 with nothing on standard output for a missing or extra file, an unknown option,
an option without its value, --column with --freq, and --top without --freq. Write one standard
error line naming the profile and frequency command forms. No --help option.
nodes.name: Parse arguments and reject malformed usage with exit 2 and a usage line.

nodes.summary: Write the profile table for every column in file order.
nodes.instructions:
Write the header column,type,rows,nulls,distinct,min,max,sum,mean,median and one row per
column in file order using encoding/csv's writer with \n line endings. Quoting follows the
writer. Nothing is written to standard output on failure.
nodes.name: Write the profile table for every column in file order.

nodes.summary: Profile only the column named by --column and exit 3 when it is absent.
nodes.instructions:
With --column, output the header and the single named column row. A name absent from the
header exits 3 with nothing on standard output.
nodes.name: Profile only the column named by --column and exit 3 when it is absent.

nodes.summary: List the most frequent values of a column ordered by count then value.
nodes.instructions:
With --freq, write the header value,count and one row per distinct non-null value ordered by
count descending, then value ascending by bytes. Nulls are not listed. An all-null column
writes only the header. An absent column name exits 3. The default limit is 5 rows.
nodes.name: List the most frequent values of a column ordered by count then value.

nodes.summary: Limit frequency rows with --top and reject non-positive values with exit 2.
nodes.instructions:
--top n lists at most n frequency rows, default 5. A value that is not a positive integer
exits 2 with nothing on standard output.
nodes.name: Limit frequency rows with --top and reject non-positive values with exit 2.

nodes.summary: Provide the POSIX bin/test.sh that runs go vet and go test.
nodes.instructions:
Write bin/test.sh in POSIX sh. From the application root it runs go vet ./... and then
go test ./..., exiting zero only when both pass. The project test suite covers each type, each
statistic, null handling, rounding, each output form, and each exit code, using files the tests
write themselves. Tests call cli.Run with bytes.Buffer writers.
nodes.name: Provide the POSIX bin/test.sh that runs go vet and go test.

nodes.summary: Build the csvstat executable with go build using only the standard library.
nodes.instructions:
Make go build -o <path> ./cmd/csvstat succeed from the application root with no third-party
modules. main wires os.Args, os.Stdout, and os.Stderr into cli.Run and exits with its result.
nodes.name: Build the csvstat executable with go build using only the standard library.

nodes.summary: Read the CSV file with encoding/csv and trim the header and every value.
nodes.instructions:
Read RFC 4180 CSV with encoding/csv. The first record is the header. Trim leading and trailing
spaces from every header name and every value. Do not reject invalid UTF-8. Blank lines are
skipped by encoding/csv. Keep record line numbers available for diagnostics.
nodes.name: Read the CSV file with encoding/csv and trim the header and every value.

nodes.summary: Report an unopenable or unreadable file, including a directory, with exit 1.
nodes.instructions:
A path that cannot be opened or read, including a missing file and a directory, exits 1 with
nothing on standard output and one diagnostic line on standard error. It must not panic.
nodes.name: Report an unopenable or unreadable file, including a directory, with exit 1.

nodes.summary: Classify empty, NA, N/A, and NULL values as null after trimming.
nodes.instructions:
A trimmed value is null when it is empty or equals NA, N/A, or NULL ignoring case. Every other
value is non-null. Expose the predicate for typing, counts, statistics, and frequencies.
nodes.name: Classify empty, NA, N/A, and NULL values as null after trimming.

nodes.summary: Infer the integer and number column types.
nodes.instructions:
A column is integer when every non-null value matches -?[0-9]+ and number when every non-null
value matches -?[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?. Typing considers only non-null values and picks the first
type in order integer, number, date, boolean, text that all of them satisfy.
nodes.name: Infer the integer and number column types.

nodes.summary: Infer the date column type with real calendar validation.
nodes.instructions:
A column is date when every non-null value matches YYYY-MM-DD and is a real calendar date, so
2025-02-30 is not a date. Use time.Parse with the 2006-01-02 layout plus a strict shape check.
nodes.name: Infer the date column type with real calendar validation.

nodes.summary: Compute the exact median for numeric columns.
nodes.instructions:
Sort the non-null numeric values exactly. The median is the middle value, or the mean of the
two middle values when the count is even, written with two decimals rounded half away from
zero. Other types are blank.
nodes.name: Compute the exact median for numeric columns.

nodes.summary: Count rows, nulls, and distinct non-null values for each column.
nodes.instructions:
rows counts data records, nulls counts null values, and distinct counts different non-null
values compared as exact trimmed strings.
nodes.name: Count rows, nulls, and distinct non-null values for each column.

nodes.summary: Infer the boolean, text, and empty column types.
nodes.instructions:
A column is boolean when every non-null value is true or false ignoring case, text otherwise,
and empty when it has no non-null value.
nodes.name: Infer the boolean, text, and empty column types.

nodes.summary: Compute exact sum and mean for numeric columns, rounded once half away from zero.
nodes.instructions:
Use math/big (big.Rat) for exact arithmetic. integer sum is a plain integer. number sum and
mean are written with two decimals, rounded once half away from zero from the exact value,
with a leading - when negative and no thousands separator. mean is the total divided by the
non-null count; integer mean is also two decimals. Other types are blank.
nodes.name: Compute exact sum and mean for numeric columns, rounded once half away from zero.

nodes.summary: Report min and max for every column type.
nodes.instructions:
integer and number compare numerically using exact math/big values and are written as plain
integers or two-decimal numbers. date gives earliest and latest. boolean gives false if any
value is false else true for min, and true if any value is true else false for max. text
compares by byte value. empty is blank.
nodes.name: Report min and max for every column type.

nodes.summary: Reject empty, malformed, or ragged files with exit 3 and a diagnostic on standard error.
nodes.instructions:
Reject an empty file, an empty or repeated header name, and any record whose field count differs
from the header. Exit 3, write nothing to standard output, and write one standard error line
naming the file and, for a record, its line number. A csv.ParseError is also a rejection.
nodes.name: Reject empty, malformed, or ragged files with exit 3 and a diagnostic on standard error.

nodes.summary: Parse arguments and reject malformed usage with exit 2 and a usage line.
nodes.instructions:
Use a local flag.FlagSet with flag.ContinueOnError and discarded flag output. Options precede
the file. Exit 2 with nothing on standard output for a missing or extra file, an unknown option,
an option without its value, --column with --freq, and --top without --freq. Write one standard
error line naming the profile and frequency command forms. No --help option.
nodes.name: Parse arguments and reject malformed usage with exit 2 and a usage line.

nodes.summary: Write the profile table for every column in file order.
nodes.instructions:
Write the header column,type,rows,nulls,distinct,min,max,sum,mean,median and one row per
column in file order using encoding/csv's writer with \n line endings. Quoting follows the
writer. Nothing is written to standard output on failure.
nodes.name: Write the profile table for every column in file order.

nodes.summary: Profile only the column named by --column and exit 3 when it is absent.
nodes.instructions:
With --column, output the header and the single named column row. A name absent from the
header exits 3 with nothing on standard output.
nodes.name: Profile only the column named by --column and exit 3 when it is absent.

nodes.summary: List the most frequent values of a column ordered by count then value.
nodes.instructions:
With --freq, write the header value,count and one row per distinct non-null value ordered by
count descending, then value ascending by bytes. Nulls are not listed. An all-null column
writes only the header. An absent column name exits 3. The default limit is 5 rows.
nodes.name: List the most frequent values of a column ordered by count then value.

nodes.summary: Limit frequency rows with --top and reject non-positive values with exit 2.
nodes.instructions:
--top n lists at most n frequency rows, default 5. A value that is not a positive integer
exits 2 with nothing on standard output.
nodes.name: Limit frequency rows with --top and reject non-positive values with exit 2.

nodes.summary: Provide the POSIX bin/test.sh that runs go vet and go test.
nodes.instructions:
Write bin/test.sh in POSIX sh. From the application root it runs go vet ./... and then
go test ./..., exiting zero only when both pass. The project test suite covers each type, each
statistic, null handling, rounding, each output form, and each exit code, using files the tests
write themselves. Tests call cli.Run with bytes.Buffer writers.
nodes.name: Provide the POSIX bin/test.sh that runs go vet and go test.

acceptance.intent: A named column yields the profile header plus exactly the row the full profile gives that column.
A column whose value contains a comma is quoted by the writer and parses back to the same row as the full profile.
A column name missing from the header exits 3 and writes nothing to standard output.
The column name is matched against trimmed header names, so a padded header still resolves.
Frequencies list non-null trimmed values by count descending then byte-ordered value, matching counts computed from the input file.
Values with equal counts are ordered ascending by byte value.
Null values are not listed, and counts equal the non-null occurrences in the file.
Without --top at most five rows are written, even when more distinct values exist.
A column with no non-null values writes only the header and exits 0.
An absent column name exits 3 with nothing on standard output.
--top n lists the first n rows of the full ordering, and a larger n lists every distinct value.
--top may precede --freq and still limits the listing.
A --top value that is not a positive integer exits 2 and writes nothing to standard output.
--top without --freq exits 2 and writes nothing to standard output.
--top given as the last option without a value exits 2.

nodes.summary: Build the csvstat executable with go build using only the standard library.
nodes.instructions:
Make go build -o <path> ./cmd/csvstat succeed from the application root with no third-party
modules. main wires os.Args, os.Stdout, and os.Stderr into cli.Run and exits with its result.
nodes.name: Build the csvstat executable with go build using only the standard library.

nodes.summary: Read the CSV file with encoding/csv and trim the header and every value.
nodes.instructions:
Read RFC 4180 CSV with encoding/csv. The first record is the header. Trim leading and trailing
spaces from every header name and every value. Do not reject invalid UTF-8. Blank lines are
skipped by encoding/csv. Keep record line numbers available for diagnostics.
nodes.name: Read the CSV file with encoding/csv and trim the header and every value.

nodes.summary: Report an unopenable or unreadable file, including a directory, with exit 1.
nodes.instructions:
A path that cannot be opened or read, including a missing file and a directory, exits 1 with
nothing on standard output and one diagnostic line on standard error. It must not panic.
nodes.name: Report an unopenable or unreadable file, including a directory, with exit 1.

nodes.summary: Classify empty, NA, N/A, and NULL values as null after trimming.
nodes.instructions:
A trimmed value is null when it is empty or equals NA, N/A, or NULL ignoring case. Every other
value is non-null. Expose the predicate for typing, counts, statistics, and frequencies.
nodes.name: Classify empty, NA, N/A, and NULL values as null after trimming.

nodes.summary: Infer the integer and number column types.
nodes.instructions:
A column is integer when every non-null value matches -?[0-9]+ and number when every non-null
value matches -?[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?. Typing considers only non-null values and picks the first
type in order integer, number, date, boolean, text that all of them satisfy.
nodes.name: Infer the integer and number column types.

nodes.summary: Infer the date column type with real calendar validation.
nodes.instructions:
A column is date when every non-null value matches YYYY-MM-DD and is a real calendar date, so
2025-02-30 is not a date. Use time.Parse with the 2006-01-02 layout plus a strict shape check.
nodes.name: Infer the date column type with real calendar validation.

nodes.summary: Compute the exact median for numeric columns.
nodes.instructions:
Sort the non-null numeric values exactly. The median is the middle value, or the mean of the
two middle values when the count is even, written with two decimals rounded half away from
zero. Other types are blank.

integers or two-decimal numbers. date gives earliest and latest. boolean gives false if any

nodes.summary: Read the CSV file with encoding/csv and trim the header and every value.
nodes.instructions:
Read RFC 4180 CSV with encoding/csv. The first record is the header. Trim leading and trailing
spaces from every header name and every value. Do not reject invalid UTF-8. Blank lines are
skipped by encoding/csv. Keep record line numbers available for diagnostics.
nodes.name: Read the CSV file with encoding/csv and trim the header and every value.

nodes.summary: Report an unopenable or unreadable file, including a directory, with exit 1.
nodes.instructions:
A path that cannot be opened or read, including a missing file and a directory, exits 1 with
nothing on standard output and one diagnostic line on standard error. It must not panic.
nodes.name: Report an unopenable or unreadable file, including a directory, with exit 1.

nodes.summary: Classify empty, NA, N/A, and NULL values as null after trimming.
nodes.instructions:
A trimmed value is null when it is empty or equals NA, N/A, or NULL ignoring case. Every other
value is non-null. Expose the predicate for typing, counts, statistics, and frequencies.
nodes.name: Classify empty, NA, N/A, and NULL values as null after trimming.

nodes.summary: Infer the integer and number column types.
nodes.instructions:
A column is integer when every non-null value matches -?[0-9]+ and number when every non-null
value matches -?[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?. Typing considers only non-null values and picks the first
type in order integer, number, date, boolean, text that all of them satisfy.
nodes.name: Infer the integer and number column types.

nodes.summary: Infer the date column type with real calendar validation.
nodes.instructions:
A column is date when every non-null value matches YYYY-MM-DD and is a real calendar date, so
2025-02-30 is not a date. Use time.Parse with the 2006-01-02 layout plus a strict shape check.
nodes.name: Infer the date column type with real calendar validation.

nodes.summary: Compute the exact median for numeric columns.
nodes.instructions:
Sort the non-null numeric values exactly. The median is the middle value, or the mean of the
two middle values when the count is even, written with two decimals rounded half away from
zero. Other types are blank.
nodes.name: Compute the exact median for numeric columns.

nodes.summary: Count rows, nulls, and distinct non-null values for each column.
nodes.instructions:
rows counts data records, nulls counts null values, and distinct counts different non-null
values compared as exact trimmed strings.
nodes.name: Count rows, nulls, and distinct non-null values for each column.

nodes.summary: Infer the boolean, text, and empty column types.
nodes.instructions:
A column is boolean when every non-null value is true or false ignoring case, text otherwise,
and empty when it has no non-null value.
nodes.name: Infer the boolean, text, and empty column types.

nodes.summary: Compute exact sum and mean for numeric columns, rounded once half away from zero.
nodes.instructions:
Use math/big (big.Rat) for exact arithmetic. integer sum is a plain integer. number sum and
mean are written with two decimals, rounded once half away from zero from the exact value,
with a leading - when negative and no thousands separator. mean is the total divided by the
non-null count; integer mean is also two decimals. Other types are blank.
nodes.name: Compute exact sum and mean for numeric columns, rounded once half away from zero.

nodes.summary: Report min and max for every column type.
nodes.instructions:
integer and number compare numerically using exact math/big values and are written as plain
integers or two-decimal numbers. date gives earliest and latest. boolean gives false if any
value is false else true for min, and true if any value is true else false for max. text
compares by byte value. empty is blank.
nodes.name: Report min and max for every column type.

nodes.summary: Reject empty, malformed, or ragged files with exit 3 and a diagnostic on standard error.
nodes.instructions:
Reject an empty file, an empty or repeated header name, and any record whose field count differs
from the header. Exit 3, write nothing to standard output, and write one standard error line
naming the file and, for a record, its line number. A csv.ParseError is also a rejection.
nodes.name: Reject empty, malformed, or ragged files with exit 3 and a diagnostic on standard error.

nodes.summary: Parse arguments and reject malformed usage with exit 2 and a usage line.
nodes.instructions:
Use a local flag.FlagSet with flag.ContinueOnError and discarded flag output. Options precede
the file. Exit 2 with nothing on standard output for a missing or extra file, an unknown option,
an option without its value, --column with --freq, and --top without --freq. Write one standard
error line naming the profile and frequency command forms. No --help option.
nodes.name: Parse arguments and reject malformed usage with exit 2 and a usage line.

nodes.summary: Write the profile table for every column in file order.

Write the header column,type,rows,nulls,distinct,min,max,sum,mean,median and one row per
column in file order using encoding/csv's writer with \n line endings. Quoting follows the
writer. Nothing is written to standard output on failure.
nodes.name: Write the profile table for every column in file order.

nodes.summary: Profile only the column named by --column and exit 3 when it is absent.

With --column, output the header and the single named column row. A name absent from the

nodes.name: Profile only the column named by --column and exit 3 when it is absent.

nodes.summary: List the most frequent values of a column ordered by count then value.

The column name is matched against trimmed header names, so a padded header still resolves.
Frequencies list non-null trimmed values by count descending then byte-ordered value, matching counts computed from the input file.
Values with equal counts are ordered ascending by byte value.
Null values are not listed, and counts equal the non-null occurrences in the file.
Without --top at most five rows are written, even when more distinct values exist.
A column with no non-null values writes only the header and exits 0.
An absent column name exits 3 with nothing on standard output.
--top n lists the first n rows of the full ordering, and a larger n lists every distinct value.
--top may precede --freq and still limits the listing.
A --top value that is not a positive integer exits 2 and writes nothing to standard output.
--top without --freq exits 2 and writes nothing to standard output.
--top given as the last option without a value exits 2.
